The annual report states Adjusted Corporate EBITDA on the earlier definition while the 2026 quarterly reports recast only 2025 interim periods on a revised one, so no consistent twelve-month figure is established. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

Leverage multiples on EBITDA are not stated for FY2024, FY2025 or 2026-09-30, because the issuer's Adjusted Corporate EBITDA was negative in both fiscal years and is not comparable for the last twelve months; this restricts every leverage, cover and covenant-style conclusion. Severity: High. Action: use a recast FY2025 figure or the fourth-quarter 2026 report on the revised definition, and read leverage on the non-vehicle layer separately. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

The fiscal-year figures use the earlier definition of Adjusted Corporate EBITDA while the 2025 comparatives in the 2026 reports are recast, so no last-twelve-months or fourth-quarter 2025 figure on one definition can be formed from the supplied reports. Severity: High. Action: obtain the recast FY2025 figure, and until then keep the two definitions in separate columns. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_47129-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 10; 10-Q_2026-03-31_47129-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is not supplied for any period and ratios on reported EBITDA are not stated; a literal derivation is shown only as an illustration in the conflict register. Severity: Medium. Action: decide whether a literal-add-back EBITDA is wanted beside the issuer's measure. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134

The effect on net debt of the Hertz cash contribution to Oro and of the Exchangeable Notes repurchase is not established, because the filing does not state whether Oro remains consolidated or the carrying value of the notes repurchased, and the October 2026 day of each event is not stated. Severity: Medium. Action: read the fourth-quarter 2026 report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59

No source states the relative legal rank of the facilities, so the debt stack is not drawn and Ranking is not supplied for any instrument. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the credit agreement, the indentures and the intercreditor terms. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

Carrying values are not stated by instrument except for the three exchangeable note lines, and security, reference rates, margins, floors and scheduled amortisation are not stated for most instruments, including the Term Loans, the Senior Notes Due 2026 and 2029 and the vehicle series. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the instrument documents or read the instrument-level terms from the executed agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–24

The First Lien RCF commitment of USD 1,700 million stated after June 2026 does not equal drawings of USD 750 million, letters of credit of USD 500 million and remaining capacity of USD 415 million, which sum to USD 1,665 million, a difference of USD 35 million that the filing does not explain. Severity: Low. Action: confirm the commitment in the next filing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26

Lines the statements print only in some periods, or print as a dash, are carried as missing values and not as zero, including the gain on sale of non-vehicle capital assets in Q3 2026, the legal settlement in FY2024, the long-lived assets impairment in FY2025, the bankruptcy-related litigation reserve in the interim periods and several cash flow lines. Severity: Low. Action: none is needed unless a later report states the amounts. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 134–136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10

Discrete first and second quarter 2026 columns are not built, the third-quarter columns cover the income statement only, cash flows are year-to-date, and the 2025-09-30 balance sheet is not in the sources, so net debt at that date is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: build the discrete quarters from the second-quarter report if a quarterly cash flow view is needed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10

Average Vehicles and the rates derived from it changed definition in Q1 2026, so utilization and depreciation per unit per month are shown on two rows, and the fiscal-year and nine-month series are not joined. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a recast fiscal-year series is published. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_47129-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80

Vehicle facilities in other currencies are printed in USD millions with no denomination amounts or rates, the nine-month and Q3 statements are unaudited. Severity: Low. Action: none unless the next audited report restates them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Hertz is a scaled, long-established vehicle rental operator whose creditors depend less on the franchise than on fleet-cost control, asset-backed funding and a sponsor-controlled owner, so governance and fleet economics are the swing factors for the credit.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: The Plan Sponsors hold more than 50% of the parent's common stock and can decide matters put to stockholders, the whole executive team joined in 2024 or 2025, the issuer's own board is three executives with no independent directors, and in 2026 the company raised first-lien exchangeable debt at an effective cost of about 17.5% and agreed an Oro Mobility joint venture in which sponsor-affiliated funds are counterparties. Revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, which supports the operating franchise. Revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, which supports the operating franchise.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business model is broad but capital intensive: two segments, three brands and a large airport and off-airport network, with Americas RAC at 79.48% of FY2025 revenue and off-airport rentals at 34% of rental revenue, while the fleet is financed by asset-backed programs and concession fees carry fixed minimums, so volume or residual-value shocks hit cash before earnings recover. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20; calculation R1

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control sits with the Plan Sponsors rather than with public stockholders or independent directors: they held more than 50% of the parent's common stock at 2025-12-31, the issuer's three-person board consists of executive officers, and the issuer has no audit, compensation or nominating committee, so creditors rely on contractual covenants and public-company controls at the parent more than on board independence at the issuer. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the operating recovery and the access to funding: revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, Americas RAC total revenue per day rose to USD 61.24 from USD 56.75, the average holding period in Americas RAC fell over 25% to 18 months with a younger fleet, and the company renewed asset-backed programs and issued four new vehicle series in 2026. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The 2026 financing program moved toward secured and exchangeable instruments. In June 2026 the issuer sold USD 350 million of exchangeable first-lien secured PIK notes due 2030 and added USD 30 million under the greenshoe in July 2026, for USD 380 million at 6.75%, half paid in cash and half in kind, with an effective interest rate of about 17.5%; the parent lent a block of its shares to an underwriter under a share lending agreement, whose initial fair value of USD 85 million the parent recorded as a debt issuance cost. The notes are first-lien secured by their stated name and so rank ahead in security of the unsecured exchangeable notes of USD 425 million issued in September 2025, but the filings do not state their rank against the first-lien senior secured notes of USD 1,250 million. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The franchise is large and long-established, with three brands, an extensive airport and off-airport network and 34% of rental revenue from off-airport locations that reduce reliance on air travel, which supports revenue durability through cycles. Vehicle debt is secured on a fleet carried at more than the debt and has been extended, which gives funding stability that earnings alone would not. facts.label: Business and ownership assessment
facts.text: The business model supports cash-flow visibility only partly: rental demand is seasonal and tied to airline travel, concessions carry fixed minimums, and the fleet must be financed ahead of revenue, but the brands, the network and off-airport rentals of 34% of rental revenue give a broad base, and the issuer is wholly owned by a parent in which the Plan Sponsors hold more than 50%, so the owner group can steer distributions and related-party dealings even though the issuer's own board has no independent oversight. Hertz Corp (The Hertz Corporation, issuer-47129), the issuer in a combined filing with its parent Hertz Global Holdings, Inc., as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway, public case. Scope is source readiness of the five supplied SEC periodic filings for the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work; no credit conclusion is drawn here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Hertz filings are enough to run the financial, business and fundamental credit work on The Hertz Corporation, but only inside stated limits, so creditors should not rely on any leverage, covenant or ratings conclusion that ignores them.

Three limits matter most. The annual report states Adjusted Corporate EBITDA on the earlier definition while the 2026 quarterly reports recast only 2025 interim periods on a revised one, so no consistent twelve-month figure is established. The parent company's debt and results differ from the issuer's, so only the issuer's own statements should carry debt and earnings. The Oro Mobility joint venture and a segment revision due in the fourth quarter of 2026 fall after the latest balance sheet, and the newest filing is 13 days older than the as-of date. No executed agreements, ratings or dated debt quotes were supplied.

spans.text: ## Request

Hertz Corp (The Hertz Corporation, issuer-47129), the issuer in a combined filing with its parent Hertz Global Holdings, Inc., as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the Financial foundation of the issuer's own statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied SEC periodic filings; no credit recommendation is made here.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Hertz's own Adjusted Corporate EBITDA was negative in both fiscal years and is not comparable for the last twelve months, so leverage multiples cannot be stated and creditors must judge the credit on liquidity, fleet collateral and cash flow.

Net debt rose from USD 15,744 million at FY2024 to USD 17,462 million at 2026-09-30 (USD 17,381 million pro forma for the cash received in the October 2026 Oro Mobility joint venture sale), while cash and available facilities fell from USD 1,842 million to USD 946 million. Vehicle debt of USD 11,958 million is matched to a fleet carried at USD 12,967 million; the earnings-dependent exposure is the non-vehicle debt of USD 6,035 million.

### Credit read-through of the figures

Net debt rose by USD 745 million in FY2025 and by USD 973 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, reaching USD 17,462 million (USD 17,381 million pro forma for the October 2026 Oro Mobility cash receipt). The issuer's Adjusted Corporate EBITDA was USD -1,541 million in FY2024 and USD -339 million in FY2025 on the earlier definition, so no ratio of debt to EBITDA exists; on the revised definition it was USD 153 million for the nine months of 2026 against USD -82 million for the recast nine months of 2025, but the two definitions cannot be joined into a last-twelve-months figure.

Basis: calculation ND1; calculation ND2; calculation ND3; calculation ND4; calculation ND5; calculation PF1; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

Vehicle debt of USD 11,958 million is 0.92x the carrying value of the revenue earning fleet of USD 12,967 million (0.94x at FY2024 and 0.93x at FY2025), so most of the debt is matched to the fleet that is its collateral. The earnings-dependent exposure is the non-vehicle debt of USD 6,035 million, up from USD 5,104 million at FY2024, and industrial leverage on it is not calculable while EBITDA is negative.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation VF1; calculation VF2; calculation VF3

Cash interest paid was USD 1,004 million in FY2025 and USD 813 million in the nine months of 2026, and cover on Adjusted Corporate EBITDA is -1.93x for FY2024 and -0.34x for FY2025. Operating cash flow of USD 1,628 million in FY2025 and USD 1,000 million in the nine months of 2026 does not cover fleet and capital spending: free cash flow was USD -366 million for FY2025 and USD -1,026 million for the nine months, and net financing inflows of USD 370 million and USD 991 million covered nearly all of it, with the net change in cash and restricted cash at USD 35 million and USD -44 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation CI1; calculation CV1; calculation CV2; calculation FC2; calculation FC4

Cash of USD 531 million and availability of USD 415 million give USD 946 million at 2026-09-30, against USD 1,842 million at FY2024. The drawn First Lien RCF rose by USD 355 million in the nine months, and the January 2026 payment of USD 346 million in the Wells Fargo case was funded from it. Nominal maturities are USD 1,475 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 2,038 million for 2027, of which vehicle debt is USD 1,272 million and USD 2,020 million, so near-term refinancing depends on renewing the asset-backed programs more than on corporate cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 208; calculation LQ1; calculation LQ3; calculation RF1; calculation LD1; calculation LD2

The October 2026 Oro Mobility events are kept out of period figures: cash of about USD 81 million from the JV Investors lowers net debt to USD 17,381 million pro forma, but the USD 60 million contributed by Hertz and the repurchase of USD 51 million of principal of the Exchangeable Notes Due 2029 for USD 21 million cannot be placed because the filing does not say whether Oro stays consolidated or what carrying value leaves debt. Debt has three figures for three purposes: the carrying value of USD 17,993 million for net debt, the principal of USD 18,300 million for maturities, and the parent's USD 17,911 million for context only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59; calculation PF1; calculation RC1; calculation PX1

The strongest contrary evidence is the 2026 improvement on the revised definition: Adjusted Corporate EBITDA of USD 233 million in Q3 2026 against USD 203 million in Q3 2025 and USD 153 million for the nine months against USD -82 million, which lifts nine-month cover from -0.11x to 0.19x. It would carry the view if the fourth-quarter 2026 report or a recast FY2025 figure gives a positive twelve-month measure; until then the negative measure means creditors rely on collateral cover, liquidity and access to the asset-backed and corporate markets.

No customer deposits, deferred revenue, supplier finance or factoring line was found in the annual or third-quarter reports, and vehicle accounts payable of USD 209 million is the only supplier credit tied to fleet purchases. Interim figures are unaudited, source dashes are carried as missing rather than zero, and the legal rank of the facilities is not stated by any supplied source.

Scope is the business, ownership, governance, capital allocation and transaction facts of the issuer from the five supplied SEC periodic filings; no credit recommendation is made here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Hertz is a scaled, long-established vehicle rental operator whose creditors depend less on the franchise than on fleet-cost control, asset-backed funding and a sponsor-controlled owner, so governance and fleet economics are the swing factors for the credit.

The Plan Sponsors hold more than 50% of the parent's common stock and can decide matters put to stockholders, the whole executive team joined in 2024 or 2025, the issuer's own board is three executives with no independent directors, and in 2026 the company raised first-lien exchangeable debt at an effective cost of about 17.5% and agreed an Oro Mobility joint venture in which sponsor-affiliated funds are counterparties. Revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, which supports the operating franchise.
### Key findings

The business model is broad but capital intensive: two segments, three brands and a large airport and off-airport network, with Americas RAC at 79.48% of FY2025 revenue and off-airport rentals at 34% of rental revenue, while the fleet is financed by asset-backed programs and concession fees carry fixed minimums, so volume or residual-value shocks hit cash before earnings recover.

Control sits with the Plan Sponsors rather than with public stockholders or independent directors: they held more than 50% of the parent's common stock at 2025-12-31, the issuer's three-person board consists of executive officers, and the issuer has no audit, compensation or nominating committee, so creditors rely on contractual covenants and public-company controls at the parent more than on board independence at the issuer.

Management is new in role: all six executive officers joined and took their current roles between April 2024 and October 2025, including the chief executive and chief financial officers, so the strategy has a short track record under this team.

Capital allocation toward owners has been restrained recently but was not in 2023: the issuer paid USD 13 million of dividends to its parent in 2025 and USD 7 million in 2024, against USD 321 million in 2023 that funded share repurchases, no repurchases were made in 2025 or 2024, and USD 874 million of the repurchase authorization remains, so the policy can change quickly.

Sponsor-related transactions are growing in 2026: sponsor-affiliated funds contributed about USD 39 million of the USD 81 million paid for Oro units and agreed to sell about USD 51 million of principal of the Exchangeable Notes Due 2029 for about USD 21 million, a discount that benefits the issuer but is struck with related parties, while investors affiliated with CK Amarillo, an affiliate of the parent, had earlier bought about USD 44 million of those notes and received a consent fee of about USD 1 million.

Funding in 2026 moved toward more expensive and more secured instruments: the first-lien exchangeable notes of USD 380 million carry an effective interest rate of about 17.5% and the second-lien exchangeable notes about 17.0%, which adds secured claims ahead of the unsecured notes and raises cash interest, and a securities class action alleges the June 2026 capital raise followed misleading liquidity statements.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the operating recovery and the access to funding: revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, Americas RAC total revenue per day rose to USD 61.24 from USD 56.75, the average holding period in Americas RAC fell over 25% to 18 months with a younger fleet, and the company renewed asset-backed programs and issued four new vehicle series in 2026. The view would turn more favourable if the proxy statement showed independent committees at the parent, if the Oro and repurchase terms were shown to be approved by disinterested directors, and if the fourth-quarter 2026 report confirmed that the joint venture reduces net debt; it would turn less favourable if sponsor-affiliated parties received further value from the issuer ahead of creditors.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not in the set, so the parent's board composition, committee independence and the sponsors' board seats are not established; this limits the conclusion that governance is sponsor-led to the issuer's own board and the stated stock ownership.

- Individual percentages of Apollo, Knighthead and Certares and of public stockholders are not stated, so the strength of any single sponsor's control and the scale of public float are not established.

- The Oro Mobility joint venture terms are summarised only in the quarterly report; the Hertz remaining stake, consolidation treatment and board approval process are not stated, which limits any conclusion on whether the repurchase discount was arm's length.
- Customer, manufacturer and business-versus-leisure mix appear only in charts that the supplied text does not carry, so no concentration conclusion is drawn.
- Evidence ends on 2026-11-05, so ownership, management and financing events after that date are not established.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2026 financing program moved toward secured and exchangeable instruments. In June 2026 the issuer sold USD 350 million of exchangeable first-lien secured PIK notes due 2030 and added USD 30 million under the greenshoe in July 2026, for USD 380 million at 6.75%, half paid in cash and half in kind, with an effective interest rate of about 17.5%; the parent lent a block of its shares to an underwriter under a share lending agreement, whose initial fair value of USD 85 million the parent recorded as a debt issuance cost. The notes are first-lien secured by their stated name and so rank ahead in security of the unsecured exchangeable notes of USD 425 million issued in September 2025, but the filings do not state their rank against the first-lien senior secured notes of USD 1,250 million.

Vehicle funding was renewed rather than reduced: in 2026 the vehicle financing subsidiary issued four new series, USD 500 million and USD 500 million in May and USD 375 million and USD 500 million in August, added USD 221 million of Class E notes in April, and extended the maturity of the Series 2021-A Class A notes to May 2028. Amendment No. 3 on 2026-11-02 extends the Class B commitment to November 2028 at a fixed 12.46%, but funding of those notes requires the senior notes due 2026 to be paid off before 2026-12-31, which links asset-backed capacity to a corporate maturity.

The Oro Mobility joint venture is the main ownership transaction: in October 2026 outside investors, including funds affiliated with Certares or Knighthead, agreed to buy Class A common units of Oro from Hertz for about USD 81 million, which gives them 50% of the voting units and about 16% of the common units, while Hertz contributed about USD 60 million of cash, assigned a 5% interest to an affiliate and keeps three of six board seats; Hertz also agreed to buy back about USD 51 million of principal of the Exchangeable Notes Due 2029 for about USD 21 million and will lease Oro vehicles at about USD 14 million a month on an average term of about 4.5 years.

Asset sales are a second funding source: sale-leasebacks of operating sites and an airport location gave gains of USD 64 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 128 million in the nine months of 2025, with the buildings portions carried as financial liabilities, and the company expects to continue them through 2026.

spans.text: ## Request

Hertz Corp (The Hertz Corporation, issuer-47129), the issuer in a combined filing with its parent Hertz Global Holdings, Inc., as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit synthesis of the issuer from the supplied SEC periodic filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs; no security recommendation or sizing is made here.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Hertz's fundamental credit profile is weak: scale, matched vehicle funding and improving 2026 pricing support it, but negative adjusted EBITDA, negative free cash flow and thin corporate liquidity mean creditors depend on fleet collateral and refinancing access rather than on earnings.

Net debt was USD 17,462 million at 2026-09-30 (USD 17,381 million pro forma for the cash received in the October 2026 Oro Mobility joint venture), cash and available facilities were USD 946 million against USD 1,475 million of maturities for the rest of 2026, and free cash flow was USD -1,026 million in the nine months. The primary downside is a further fall in used-vehicle values, which would raise depreciation and collateral calls while corporate liquidity is already below its FY2024 and FY2025 levels.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F5; calculation F6
### Key findings

Earnings do not yet cover the cost of capital: Adjusted Corporate EBITDA was USD -1,541 million in FY2024 and USD -339 million in FY2025 on the earlier definition, giving interest cover of -1.93x and -0.34x, and although the revised definition shows USD 153 million for the nine months of 2026 against USD -82 million a year earlier, no comparable twelve-month figure exists, so leverage multiples are not meaningful.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7; calculation F8

Cash generation is positive before fleet spending but negative after it: operating cash flow was USD 1,628 million in FY2025 and USD 1,000 million in the nine months of 2026, yet free cash flow was USD -366 million and USD -1,026 million, and net debt rose USD 973 million in the nine months, so the business consumes capital while it rebuilds earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5; calculation F9

The debt structure is more collateralised than the headline suggests: vehicle debt of USD 11,958 million is 0.92x the fleet carried at USD 12,967 million, so the earnings-dependent exposure is the non-vehicle debt of USD 6,035 million, which has risen from USD 5,104 million and was refinanced in 2026 with first-lien exchangeable notes at an effective rate of about 17.5%.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F11

Liquidity is the binding constraint: cash of USD 531 million and availability of USD 415 million total USD 946 million, down from USD 1,842 million at FY2024, against USD 1,475 million of maturities in the rest of 2026 and USD 2,038 million in 2027, nearly all vehicle debt, and the Class B vehicle commitment extended in November 2026 funds only if the senior notes due 2026 are repaid by 2026-12-31.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 93; calculation F3; calculation F4

Governance adds a creditor-alignment risk without clear offsetting controls: the Plan Sponsors hold more than 50% of the parent's common stock, the issuer's board is three executives with no committees, all six executive officers joined in 2024 or 2025, and 2026 brought related-party dealings with sponsor-affiliated funds and securities litigation over the June capital raise.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 213–214
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is the 2026 operating turn: revenue rose 8.35% in the nine months, quarterly Adjusted Corporate EBITDA was USD 233 million in Q3 2026 against USD 203 million in Q3 2025, the vehicle funding programs were renewed with four new series, and fleet rotation cut the Americas holding period to 18 months. The view would improve if the fourth-quarter 2026 report gives a positive twelve-month measure on the revised definition, if used-vehicle prices hold so that depreciation per unit stays near USD 301 a month, and if the 2026 senior notes are repaid without new secured debt; it would worsen if corporate liquidity falls below USD 946 million, if collateral calls arise, or if further value passes to sponsor-affiliated parties.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 71; calculation F2; calculation F8
### Limitations
- No credit rating, agency report or dated debt quote is supplied, so the weak overall assessment is not tested against rating or market views and could be harsher or more lenient than they imply.

- No twelve-month earnings measure on one definition exists, so the 2026 improvement cannot be annualised and the conclusion that earnings do not cover the cost of capital would soften if a positive twelve-month figure appears.

- Executed financing documents are not supplied, so rank, security and covenant headroom of each instrument are not established and the collateral-cover conclusion rests on the filings' own summaries.
- The October 2026 joint venture and the segment revision from the fourth quarter of 2026 are not in period figures, so the business perimeter assessed here may differ from the one reported next.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The franchise is large and long-established, with three brands, an extensive airport and off-airport network and 34% of rental revenue from off-airport locations that reduce reliance on air travel, which supports revenue durability through cycles. Vehicle debt is secured on a fleet carried at more than the debt and has been extended, which gives funding stability that earnings alone would not. Pricing drove revenue up 8.35% in the nine months of 2026, and Adjusted Corporate EBITDA turned positive on the revised definition.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_47129-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15; calculation F2

Weaknesses. Earnings measures were negative in both fiscal years, free cash flow is negative after fleet spending, corporate liquidity of USD 946 million is small against near-term maturities, and funding has become more secured and more expensive, with an effective rate of about 17.5% on the 2026 first-lien exchangeable notes. Sponsor control above 50%, a three-executive issuer board and related-party transactions raise creditor-alignment risk, and used-vehicle price softness and securities litigation add event risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49

### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
The registers and sections below carry the evidence behind the passages above; each table cell states its source.
### Business and ownership assessment

The business model supports cash-flow visibility only partly: rental demand is seasonal and tied to airline travel, concessions carry fixed minimums, and the fleet must be financed ahead of revenue, but the brands, the network and off-airport rentals of 34% of rental revenue give a broad base, and the issuer is wholly owned by a parent in which the Plan Sponsors hold more than 50%, so the owner group can steer distributions and related-party dealings even though the issuer's own board has no independent oversight.
### Revenue durability and pricing

Revenue durability is moderate: price rather than volume drove 2026, with revenue up 8.35% in the nine months while transaction days rose by about one percent in each segment, so the recovery depends on pricing holding as used-vehicle values and demand evolve; revenue had fallen in FY2025 to USD 8,504 million from USD 9,049 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 73; calculation F2; calculation F12
### Cost structure, margin resilience and cash conversion

Margins are exposed to fleet depreciation and fixed concession and site costs: depreciation and lease charges were USD 3,611 million in FY2024 and USD 1,927 million in FY2025, which shows how large the swing is, and cash conversion is weak because fleet expenditure net of disposals exceeds operating cash flow, giving free cash flow of USD -366 million in FY2025 and USD -1,026 million in the nine months of 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5; calculation F13
### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is intense with Avis Budget Group, Enterprise Holdings and SIXT, and with ride share and peer-to-peer platforms, which limits pricing power; manufacturers supply the fleet and program vehicles shift residual risk to them at a higher purchase cost; airports and insurers act as powerful counterparties through concessions and reimbursement terms; and the move into Oro Mobility with ride share partners adds both a growth option and execution risk.
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is weak on earnings and cash flow, average on collateral and market access, and weak on policy and governance. Earnings and coverage are negative, liquidity is below its prior levels, and leverage cannot be expressed on earnings, but vehicle debt is matched to collateral and asset-backed programs were extended to 2028 and beyond, which has kept market access open at a rising cost.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25; calculation F7; calculation F10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next one to two years the tailwinds are the 2026 pricing recovery, the extended vehicle programs and the joint venture cash, and the headwinds are the USD 1,475 million of 2026 maturities, the 2026 senior notes of USD 199 million tied to the Class B condition, used-vehicle softness and the segment reorganisation; over three to five years the 2028 maturity wall of USD 7,118 million, which holds the revolver, term loans and vehicle programs, is the main refinancing test.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_47129-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 93; calculation F4; calculation F12
### Qualitative downside scenario

The most credible downside starts with a further fall in used-vehicle values, which raises depreciation and losses on vehicle sales, triggers collateral top-ups in the asset-backed facilities and absorbs cash that corporate liquidity of USD 946 million cannot easily replace; the first break would appear in depreciation per unit per month rising above its 2026 level of USD 301 in Americas RAC, the financial transmission would be lower availability and higher secured borrowing at rates near 17.5%, and the observable trigger would be a shortfall in repaying the 2026 senior notes or further first-lien exchangeable issuance.
